utterances.text: In continuation, Mr. Tokic, I'm going to ask you questions relating to examination-in-chief by Bruno Stojic's Defence. The first question refers to deserters, page 11 of yesterday's transcript. Actually, I have only one question relating to this topic. If the military conscripts from Gornji Vakuf left the area of the municipality, could the brigade command or anyone from the municipality do anything to locate these conscripts and bring them back to Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a brigade commander, as well as the civilian institutions in Uskoplje, had no jurisdiction over these matters, if a military conscript felt [as interpreted] the area of the municipality, he was deemed inaccessible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: My next question refers to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you are saying that he was no longer accessible, but this should come under the jurisdiction of the military prosecutor; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I and the authorities of Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje, he was not accessible. However, he may have been accessible to higher authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Was that precisely the reason for you, at the meeting held on the 26th of October, 1993, you made requests that you have passed on to the authorities of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said today as well that that was the ultimate cry for help that we made in order to gain more troops and more equipment in order to enable us to carry out our mission, which was the protection of Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje as well as the protection of property and people's lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Bruno Stojic's Defence asked you about item 7 from document 3D796, 3D796, and these are conclusions from the meeting held on the 26th of October. This particular item contained a request for drafting a single disciplinary rule book that would be appropriate for wartime. The this question was on page 24, and there were also Judges' questions on the same topic. Mr. Tokic, you told us that the rule book was not distributed on -- in the field but that there were guide-lines issued directing the troops how to implement this rule book. I would just like to draw your attention to some of the elements of this rule book in order for us to be able to define and determine why one of these appeals and cries for help you formulated at this meeting referred to the rule book of -- disciplinary rule book as well. In the documents that you have in your file, look at the document P293, military disciplinary rule book. Just briefly, for the Judges to get a rough picture of why you posed these requests, look at Article 6. In Article 6, it is said that: "Disciplinary errors shall be milder breaches of rules or other regulations, whereas -- as well as breaches of other enactments." Have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Look at Article 10 now, which reads: "Certain disciplinary measures can be imposed and pronounced for those who commit minor disciplinary breaches." My assistant is telling me that what I said about Article 6 was not entered into the record. Article 6 says that disciplinary errors are to be considered as milder breaches of discipline and that disciplinary breaches -- disciplinary offences shall be gross breaches of rules and discipline. From this, it derives that there are two possible ways of breaching discipline; milder and more serious. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: In Article 10, it says that for the minor breaches of discipline, the following disciplinary measures shall be pronounced. And in Article 11, that for disciplinary offences -- that is to say, for more serious breaches of discipline, disciplinary punishment can be pronounced. The book of rules, therefore, distinguishes two different sanctions for milder breaches of discipline and punishments for serious breaches of discipline; is that correct, Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's look at Chapter 3 now. I beg your pardon, Chapter 2 of this book of rules, which speaks about punishments for milder breaches of discipline. I'm going to paraphrase, and the Chamber can -- Trial Chamber can see for themselves. And it says that military commanders are entitled to impose disciplinary measures for milder breaches. Mr. Tokic, were you aware of the fact that military commanders were eligible and entitled to impose such measures for the breaches of discipline of a milder nature?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at Chapter 3 of these rules. It refers to the decision-making and deliberating on more serious breaches of discipline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Alaburic, it would be easier to find the place if you gave a number of an article rather than the chapter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so, and I'm sorry that I didn't think of that myself. Chapter 3 begins with Article 51. This chapter refers to the sanctions to be imposed for more serious breaches of discipline, and it is stipulated here that these measures shall be decided by military disciplinary courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: From what we have just glanced at, it turns out that military commanders were not authorised to impose disciplinary measures on their troops for serious breaches of discipline; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I just have an objection to these questions being leading. This is not a cross-examination, this is direct examination, so in order not to get up all the time I would just like to make this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in a non-identified procedure zone, so please try and avoid -- refrain from putting leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so, and I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, at the meeting of the 26th of October, 1993, when you asked for disciplinary rules to be compiled, a single book of rules, did you ask to expand the authority of military commanders when it comes to punishing the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, among other things, asked for more authority for the military commanders, but also we asked for the system acts more efficiently in order for us to gain access to those who were inaccessible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: In that context, Judge Trechsel asked you whether these powers referred both to the soldiers who were not on duty, and I think you answer that when asked about that by General Praljak. But let me just draw your attention to one of the rules from the book of rules just to see to whom it refers. Let us look at Article 4, Mr. Tokic, which reads that these rules shall be applicable to military servicemen and civilians employed in the armed forces. And in Article 21, it says that military servicemen are defined in a more precise manner by saying that they include soldiers, reserve soldiers, officers, and non-commissioned officers. According to your knowledge, with the exception of these four categories, was there any category of servicemen?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking about the doctrine of the All People's Defence, it recognises the methodology by stating that the preparation for defence and participation in defence is realised by serving in active duty units than in reserve units, than by serving in civilian protection units, by serving in surveillance and early-warning system units. This was also stipulated as work obligation for the citizens, who should ensure that the production of food, ammunition, and everything else should go on. And, finally, there is an obligation of providing material support. That referred to the assets belonging to the citizens who, at the request of the defence office, give their personal car, their tractor, their lorry, or livestock for the use of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, now let's move on to a new area, and that area is SIS, S-I-S. Now, the questions and answers recorded in yesterday's transcript range from pages 25 onwards, and what I'm interested in covers some 10 pages of that record. Now, I'll just remind you of some of the elements. You were shown a number of documents. Questions were asked about them. And on page 26, you were asked the following: Whether the commander from the SIS Administration asked you about your opinion about the appointment of his SIS assistant. And on page 29 of the record, you were asked about your oral approval whereby the assistant SIS person for your brigade should be appointed in the SIS centre. And you were shown a document alongside the question, so would you please look at that now. It is 2D567. It is the decision on the internal establishment and organisation of the Defence Department, dated the -- dated 1992. And the Stojic Defence asked you to focus on item 4 of that decision. And I'm now going to summarise what it says here on the subject of appointments. Appointments from the first three lines of this item is done by the head of the Defence Department, at the proposal of the assistant head for security, and further down in the text it goes on to say that the operatives and lower-level employees are deployed directly by the assistant for security, along with prior approval from the head of the Defence Department. Now, my question to you, Mr. Tokic, is this: From this decision, I do not see that in this procedure -- that this procedure provided for the fact that the brigade commander should give -- state any opinion or state his agreement and approval with respect to the appointment of any person working in SIS, so can you explain to us now this discrepancy between the rules and regulations and practice?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, it is true that I in no way was consulted when it came to appointing Zvonko Katovic, my assistant for security, nor did he ask me for any kind of approval, prior approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, I apologise for interrupting you, but can you just tell us what, in your opinion, was the reason for which the procedure on appointment was stipulated in one way in the rules and regulations, whereas it worked differently in practice, which the Stojic Defence, in the presentation of its case, showed us? Can you just tell us what the reason for that was, the reason for this discrepancy and divergence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I do hesitate to rise, but I would ask -- there's been very long questions that have taken on the characteristic of almost narratives rather than direct questioning, and I would ask that particular attention be given by my learned friend not to lead. There's no rule, of course, that allows leading questions or suggestion in re-examination. The usual rules of evidence must apply, and I'd ask that my learned friend adhere to those rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, please reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just put to the witness what was stated during the cross-examination by the Stojic Defence, and my question is a simple one. Does the witness know why, in the decision, the procedure governing appointments is set up in one way, whereas things happened in quite a different way in practice? Perhaps the witness knows what the reason for that was; perhaps he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to Zvonko Katovic, Luka Markovic, as the head of the SIS centre, came to have a cup of coffee with me together with Zvonko Katovic, and when asked whether I agreed that Zvonko Katovic should move over to -- right in the SIS centre, I said that I did agree, that I gave my approval. Now, further procedure, as brigade commander, I did not know what the subsequent procedure was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, in reading item 4 here, if you read it carefully, all it deals with is the question of appointment, appointment for SIS workers, whereas there's not a single word about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I do object. Once again, my learned friend is interposing, with a question, her own interpretation of a document. This is inappropriate, so that's one of the grounds of the objection. The other, Your Honour, is that I would ask that my learned friend, when she wishes to ask further questions, in order to assist the Chamber, gives the reference as to the portion of my learned friend Ms. Nozica's questioning, and so she can say that, On page X, on line so-and-so, you were asked this, and so it's very clear what the re-examination is said to arise out of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you put a very specific question to the witness. You asked him whether he knew why, in the text, there was a procedure and that the practice was different. He's telling you -- well, actually, he's mentioning two cases, the Luka Markovic and Zvonko Katovic, where he was asked -- about whom he was asked his advice, and the rest he doesn't know. Well, then that's it, there's no need to continue. What more do you want? He's just told you that he doesn't know. Isn't that enough? And the text is very clear. The text does show that these people were not appointed on an intervention from the brigade commander. You're wasting time. What more do you want? You're not adding anything, you're not adding any value. I could cut you off right now. I'm too lenient, you know, so I let you go on, but it's pointless. You're wasting your time, it's fruitless, plus you're raising problems with other Defence teams. On a legal case, you know, we have a document that says this is the procedure, this is what happens in practice. He just gives us his opinion, and it can't go on any further. So now that we are done with this subject, you know, move on to something else. There's no need to, you know, to flog a dead horse.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have an objection at this point in time as to how these proceedings are being conducted. When the Stojic Defence raised questions that were not raised during the examination-in-chief, you did not utter a single word to say that they were additional questions or areas, and you never said a single word that, in keeping with your rules, that you couldn't ask questions -- you couldn't ask leading questions to new -- on new topics. Now, the way in which you're reacting to the Stojic Defence team, I really do consider that it is an infringement of the right to a fair trial, and I consider that as far as General Milivoj Petkovic is concerned, with conducting the proceedings in court in this way, I really do feel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, don't speak nonsense. You have a text. You want to know whether the SIS people are appointed with the advice of the brigade commander. I understand your point. You're defending Mr. Petkovic. I understand your purpose. You put the question to the witness. He answered, saying that as far as he was concerned, he was asked -- his opinion was asked just once, but he can't say anything more, so that's it. Why talk about a fair -- fair proceedings and so forth? I understood. We have a document, there is a specific procedure. That's it. What are you trying to prove? I don't understand your point. How is talking about a fair trial -- fair trial, fine. I want to understand your questions, but they have to have a purpose. If they go against your own interest, I will warn you and tell you that you're wasting your time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise, but may I just be allowed to respond to His Honour Judge Antonetti. Judge Antonetti, Your Honour, my last question related to the topic of dismissal of SIS personnel, dismissing them of their duties. Up until that time, we were talking about appointments. And if you want to understand document 3D796 properly, then you would have to try and understand why the military commanders, in item 13 of that document, wrote that the authorisation and remit of the manner of putting forward appointments should be established for the SIS service. Now, what I want to demonstrate was, first of all, that the regulations and procedure on appointment was set up in one way, whereas practice was different, it functioned differently in practice. And if you will allow me, Judge Antonetti, in continuation of my examination, I'll focus on other elements which are important to understand why it was that the military commanders made this conclusion in the first place. And I consider that in this courtroom, it is also very vital -- it is also important to note the tone used by the Trial Chamber and the tone used in addressing each of the Defence teams, and if there is a difference in the way in which the Trial Chamber addresses the various Defence teams, or if certain counsel, Defence counsel, are regularly -- on a regular basis interrupted in their examination, whereas others are allowed to go on and for umpteen minutes, whether they have something to say or not, I consider that to be an infringement of my right to a fair trial, and I consider it my duty to indicate this and, if necessary, that steps be taken to redress that. Now, I cede the floor to Mr. Khan, if he wishes to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm most grateful. With the greatest of respect, I deprecate any innuendo or suggestion of unfairness that's raised by my learned friend, and, of course, I'm sure it was not the case that any threat was being raised. If there is any unfairness in these proceedings, that unfairness that is alleged can be rectified at an appropriate stage before the Appeals Chamber. In my respectful submission, Your Honours have endeavoured to put forward, within the constraints that you're operating under, a fair trial to all parties. But with the greatest of respect, the submission of my learned friend is nonsense, absolute and utter nonsense, and in due course, Your Honour, we will be inviting Your Honours to give less weight to the testimony of a witness -- any witness where there is movement in re-examination, where, as in the present case, my learned friend has not only sought to reply to an objection, but has given a road map to the witness, who's in the courtroom, as to what she seeks to get from that witness. That is a gross liberty, in my respectful submission, which can only affect the credibility of a witness that you have to assess when you are assessing the evidence that is elicited. Your Honour, my learned friend raised the objection initially, at page 56, that the Defence for Bruno Stojic raised questions that were not raised in examination-in-chief. I am most perplexed by that proposition. Of course, the questions put forward by my learned friend Ms. Nozica was cross-examination, and the Rules make it very clear that questioning in cross-examination is not confined to evidence led in-chief, but is led -- can extend to any evidence that is relevant. But that's not only the case. The cross-examination that was put forward by Bruno Stojic directly arose out of Defence -- out of examination-in-chief. Your Honour, this document, 3D796, is a document that was put forward by General Praljak, and if one looks at paragraph 14, Your Honour will see that the questioning of my learned friend -- sorry, paragraph 13, paragraph 13, you'll see that the questioning of my learned friend and the Defence for Mr. Stojic arises directly -- directly out of the evidence that was put forward by General Praljak. So the proposition or the assertion that's being bandied about, that there's been some extravagant lenience that's been given to the Defence for Mr. Stojic, is singularly without a scintilla of merit, in my respectful submission. Your Honour, I would ask, without wasting further time, that my learned friend simply gets on with re-examination and confines it to issues that have arisen out of cross, and she should be quite specific as to why she says it's relevant, and should ask it in a non-leading, non-suggestive format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, please refrain from putting leading questions. You wanted to highlight two things: That there's on the one thing, the appointment, and the dismissal. So if you absolutely wish to talk about the dismissal, please put your question, but be brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will speak about dismissals, because that was the topic of the document that was shown by the Stojic Defence, and it is document 2D3053. And I will get to that in due course. This is just an introductory question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Anyway, on this -- in this decision on internal establishment, can you find a provision which deals with the dismissal of SIS employees?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, Madam Counsel, I cannot see that dismissals are governed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please now look at the next document previously shown to you by Stojic's Defence, which is 2D3053. Asking questions about this document, Bruno Stojic's Defence counsel said, which is on page 28 and onwards on page -- 27 and 28: [In English] "It is sent by the Main Staff of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna personally to Ivan Lucic." [Interpretation] My first question is: Mr. Tokic, can you tell us who sent this report?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was sent by my assistant for security, Mr. Zvonko Katovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the head of SIS in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Madam Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Tell us his name.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Mr. Ivan Lucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Can you please look at page 1 of this document. Was this document sent to Mr. Ivan Lucic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. On page 1, you see: "Main Staff of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Attention: Mr. Ivan Lucic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: So was Mr. Ivan Lucic with the Main Staff or with the Defence Ministry; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he should be with the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how come that your assistant for security doesn't know where number 1 person in SIS is stationed or where he works?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to give you an answer to that. I said that I knew that he was with the Ministry of Defence, and why Katovic said "Main Staff," probably a clerical error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, the next person -- the next recipient of this document was Luka Markesic. Mr. Tokic, did you, too, receive this report?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because this service had a special packaged radio communication which was hidden away from the commander, and the commander saw it for the first time yesterday in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Tokic, you said that your assistant for security was within your chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, he was my assistant for security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I understand that communications coming from your SIS assistant were sent without you knowing about it, but you said that this was a packet-switching system. And when I look at this in your own language, I see that this document has been signed, so these are sent by packet-switching system, and here we have a handwritten signature. So this must have been sent via mail. I don't know. There's a signature here. Katovic has signed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, allow me to explain. My assistant for security in the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade, Zvonko Katovic, was not using my line of reporting to the military district or operations zone. He had a separate modem and a separate computer, and even I, as the commander, could be unaware of some information that he was sending. And I categorically claim that this document that I'm holding in my hand now, I saw it for the first time yesterday in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I agree with what you've said, but the problem doesn't come from there. The fact is that the communication wasn't sent by modem, or via computer, or through electronic means, because the letter is signed, so this must have been placed in an envelope and, I don't know, perhaps a courier or postman brought it, or maybe a pigeon, perhaps. But this wasn't sent through electronic means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain? The SIS centre in Rama, due to security issues from the area of Rama municipality, was placed in Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje. Luka Markesic was operating from Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje, and this report was probably taken by Luka Markesic -- or, rather, sent by courier, in a car, and delivered to Mr. Ivan Lucic at the Ministry of Defence, and this could be the explanation for the signature. But this document was probably sent also through packet radio communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... now we have the explanation. I would just like to say that one word is missing in the record. Before the question asked by Judge Antonetti, the witness gave an affirmative answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, in this document, it is described in what way you dismissed and transferred a SIS desk clerk to infantry. I'm going to ask you about this issue, the following: As the head of SIS, did Ivica Lucic annul this decision on transfer to the infantry?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Counsel, nobody from the Security Service reacted to my decision, and as far as I can remember, after that this official probably left the area of Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje and went to undergo surgery in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: According to what you know, Mr. Tokic, as the head of SIS, immediately after having learned about this incident, did Mr. Lucic appoint a new desk clerk to your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Ministry of Defence intervene with regard to this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, when, at the meeting of the 26th of October, 1993, the military commanders asked the civilian authorities to pass the rule governing the authority with respect to dismissals and appointments of SIS personnel, what was their intention? What did they hope to achieve?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wished, first of all, for this procedure to be defined in a manner that everyone can understand and that should be based on the qualifications and skills of those persons rather than to be directed against the so-called whistle-blowers, and that would be something that this person can freely pass without giving an opportunity to a commander to clear his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... tell you that because of the tapes that we should, normally speaking, have a break around quarter past 12.00, 20 past 12.00. You have already had 30 minutes for your redirect, which is a fair amount of time. Maybe it would be a good idea to finish now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel, for the interruption. I apologise, Mr. President, and to counsel for the interruption. The Prosecution will have a very brief submission to make, which we'd like to do today at some point before we finish for the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a feeling that everyone is eager to complete this session today as soon as possible. Let me just check this report on SIS personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: On page 3, that's in English the middle of page 4, Mr. Katovic says as follows: "There are personnel problems in the brigade because the brigade commander has not been appointed." It turns out, Mr. Tokic, that at that point you were not the commander of the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade. Can you offer any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Counsel, what was going on in the domain of personnel issues and what personnel documents said, I didn't care much about that at the time. I had much more important duties to do and to carry out my mission, and the procedure for my appointment was not within the scope of my considerations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you only one more document, which is P4211, P4211. Please look at Article 5, which reads as follows: "The checks and the supervision of the legality of the operation of SIS shall be ensured and implemented by the head of the Defence Department and the person appointed by the president of the HZ-HB." Mr. Tokic, were you aware that these institutions were entrusted with supervising the operation of SIS?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I didn't read these rules during the war in great detail. As a commander in wartime, I had my own obligations, and I knew how to act. Therefore, I was not aware of these measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for granting me additional time. Thank you, Mr. Tokic. And for the benefit of further successful completion of this session, I will refrain from asking any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to thank you for having come to testify at the request of the Praljak and Petkovic Defence teams. I shall ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon to you and to Your Honour Judge Trechsel and all counsel. Yesterday, the Prosecution did have an opportunity to analyse the response filed by the Petkovic team -- I'm sorry, the reply filed by the Petkovic team to the response that the Prosecution had submitted in respect of a Defence motion on Rule 68 issues, and we've -- we analysed that yesterday recognising that this is exceptional. I don't remember the last time the Prosecution has asked for permission to reply to a reply, but we're asking for that now as an exceptional matter. We believe that the reply filed by the Defence fundamentally misrepresents the Prosecution position. We're troubled by the Defence reply or the response's invitation to the Trial Chamber to treat the Prosecution's submissions with skepticism, which is one of a number of statements contained in the Defence filing that is troublesome to us, we think inappropriate. In any event, we are asking, exceptionally in this situation, for the Trial Chamber's permission to file a brief written reply to that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. May I say straight away that this topic got kicked off yesterday by a reference to word limits. And just to correct the record, we all, including me, I truly confess, were under a misapprehension that the word limit was 1500 words. It was actually 3.000. So it would be churlish for me to withdraw an application that Your Honour granted, but it turns out the word limit application was actually completely unnecessary. Perhaps I should just note that. But on the substance of the matter which is now being canvassed by Mr. Stringer, and he did mention it yesterday, Your Honour, the reply -- and Your Honours now have it. It was filed yesterday. The reply very specifically, point by point, deals with specific matters raised by reference to paragraphs in the Prosecution response. It is well within the normal ambit of a reply. The skepticism to which Mr. Stringer refers is not in any way any innuendo of any lack of good faith on the part of the Prosecution. If Your Honours have had an opportunity or do have an opportunity to look at our reply, it's just a skepticism as to how the process would actually work when one looks at what everybody's obligations are. Your Honour, if this most unusual step is going to be taken, then it ought to be presented to Your Honours more specifically than this, rather than just mention a point in our reply by reference to "skepticism" and then ask for some general leave to put in a further filing. It's incumbent upon the Prosecution, we suggest, to say very specifically what it is that they wish to take up, and confine any further document very specifically to that matter, if indeed it is justified at all. So in our submission, Your Honour, this application needs to be more directly and specifically made to Your Honour and not in those rather general terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, I have just consulted my colleague on the Bench. Before we grant you leave to reply, we would like to know on what points you would like -- specifically you would like to respond to the Defence's reply. The Trial Chamber acknowledges that an extremely important point has been raised by the Defence motion, so we need all the information we can get. A lot of written submissions have been filed so far, and before we grant you leave to respond, because this would be an exceptional case, we would like to know what specific points you would like to focus on in your reply, based on the Defence written submissions. And I think you could specify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We are a bit limited in our possibilities to deliberate within the reduced Chamber. The idea I think we agreed upon was that you would, as is often done with a request to file a reply, file your request for re-reply together with the re-reply, which would give the Chamber the possibility to look at it and then decide whether to accept it or not. As you have said that you would file it tomorrow, we suppose that you are ready, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, it hasn't been written, Your Honour, but it will be, and it certainly can and would be filed tomorrow. I think the suggestion by Your Honour Judge Trechsel is certainly one that is appropriate, and we will do that. We will file this as a request to file a reply to the reply, and we will identify the specific points, and then the Trial Chamber, obviously, can accept or reject that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Obviously, there has to be some limits to this process, but may I simply say that naturally we would wish to reserve our position. And I am, I believe, speaking on behalf of the three Defences who filed the reply which has triggered off this particular discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, to understand more clearly what all this is about, let's look into the request for leave to reply, which will be filed by the Prosecution tomorrow. Next week, we shall be hearing an expert witness. This has been planned. Mr. Kovacic, your witness will be there on Monday, will he?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No, we have no problems. We have been informed that the witness is coming in as planned. We'll have a proofing session over the weekend, but otherwise he ought to be here, unless something unforeseen happens like him falling down some steps in the hotel and breaking his leg or anything of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We hope that this person will be on his two feet on Monday. I hope everybody will be on his or her feet on Monday, and I will have the pleasure of meeting you again on Monday at a quarter past 2.00. The Court stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of October, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.21 p.m.,
